title: Full Day of Eating (Lean Bulk)
summary: His first full day of eating, on an instinctive, untracked lean bulk built on high carbs, moderate protein and fairly low fat. He eats foods he enjoys in small, frequent portions and skips dairy, red meat and stimulants. He judges progress by occasional weigh-ins, how he looks and gym progression, and does a physique check at 215 lb.
claims: You don't have to eat 15 times a day or eat foods you dislike to bulk; diet is easy if you don't overcomplicate it
Breakfast is his favourite meal psychologically, so he eats sweet things he enjoys (croissants with peanut butter or blueberry jam); banning all sugar is too extreme
He avoids Nutella because of palm oil and refined sugar and prefers fruit-based sweet options
Banana test: if a banana doesn't taste very sweet to you, modern products have probably ruined your taste buds
He doesn't drink coffee or use stimulants because he sees relying on them to get going as a slippery slope
He has only one scoop of whey a day; if you need many scoops to hit protein, the rest of your diet is garbage, and a diet that is 50% supplements is wrong
He adds collagen to his oat-milk whey for tendon health, and it also helps the whey mix
His first meal is around 10:30 am after the last meal at 9 pm the night before, a de facto fast that just fits his schedule
He drinks only water (sometimes with lemon), oat milk and occasionally orange juice; no sodas or coffee
When bulking, keep portions small and split food across the day; huge meals kill appetite and many hardgainers make this mistake
He uses about 4 garlic cloves in his sardine snack; too much garlic without adapting can make you vomit
Chewing 5-6 cloves (the spice) for about 10 minutes after garlic removes the bad breath and may help liver function and blood sugar
His bulking diet is very high carb, moderate protein and moderately low fat; he thinks high protein is unnecessary
A past high-fat, high-protein, lower-carb diet was catastrophic for him; macro preferences must be found by trial and error
He avoids dairy and red meat because they make him bloated and sick, and says anyone who reacts badly to a food should drop it; no single food is required to grow
He cooks almost everything himself and gets veggies through homemade ratatouille mixed with white rice
White rice is his go-to carb because it digests easily and keeps him full through workouts
He eats mostly plants and carbs with modest animal products, and finds he performs, grows and feels healthier that way
He doesn't track calories on a bulk because tracking feeds his obsessive tendencies; tracking is still the easiest way to know if you're gaining
He weighs himself only every 2-4 weeks instead of daily for his mental health, and also judges fullness and appearance
Training progression is the number one check: bulk to perform and add volume; if training doesn't improve as calories rise, you won't grow. Training dictates diet
His instinctive approach may only work because he has a slow metabolism, so a small increase creates a surplus; hardgainers may need otherwise
A pre-workout meal should be just enough to avoid hunger without sitting heavy in the stomach, e.g. cereal and unsweetened applesauce
He takes no stimulant pre-workout because he enjoys training and shouldn't need to be amped up for it
Bland bodybuilder food is theatrics; naturals should eat tasty home-prepared food, since sacrificing enjoyment breeds eating disorders and misery
On a bulk your abs can blur, but watch your waist; a rapidly growing waist means visceral fat and a bulk going wrong
His biceps dominate his arms while triceps and shoulders lag, and he accepts that may never change
Eating the same food every day reinforces his neurotic traits, so he keeps both diet and training flexible; rigid structure breaks badly
Consistency of the surplus is key, and eating food you love is how you stay consistent, especially with a slow instinctive bulk of about a pound a month
Training matters more than diet for getting big: you can't out-train a bad diet when cutting, but no amount of food builds muscle without gym work
